criteria.criterion: Components are documented with a written design rationale (per the skill's 'What Good Looks Like' bar and Component Definition Process).
criteria.evidence: All 3 runs of eval 1 open with 'Write a Design Rationale (Before Any Naming)' / 'Write the Design Rationale (Before Any Name)' / 'Write a Design Rationale First', each giving a 1-2 sentence rationale template and calling it 'the single source of truth'. All 3 runs of eval 2 require a 'Design Rationale' field in the proposal template (e.g. run1: 'Every proposal must start with a rationale. No rationale = not ready to review.'; run3: 'This is non-negotiable. It's the single source of truth...').

criteria.criterion: Design-engineering (and cross-discipline) alignment on naming/conventions is enforced, not left to individual taste.
criteria.evidence: Eval 1 run1/run2/run3 all instruct convening designer, developer, content strategist, and maintainer before naming, and state naming 'follows naturally' from agreed purpose rather than aesthetics (run1: 'Never name from aesthetics... The rationale drives the name.'). Eval 2's review checklists in all 3 runs include a naming-convention gate (run1: 'Naming is consistent — follows the token/component naming convention'; run3: 'Proposed name aligns with your naming conventions').

criteria.criterion: A contribution model with clear per-component ownership is prescribed (who proposes/reviews/approves, and a named owner).
criteria.evidence: All 3 eval 2 runs define explicit propose/review/approve roles (run1: 'Proposer... Reviewers... Approver... Maintainer'; run2: 'Who can propose... Who reviews... Who approves') and assign a named owner per component (run1's owner table; run2: 'Each component must have a named owner — not a committee'; run3: 'Assign owners to pairs (one designer, one engineer)').

criteria.criterion: Accessibility is treated as baked into the component/design definition up front, not bolted on after the fact.
criteria.evidence: Accessibility appears only inconsistently and mostly as a late-stage checklist item rather than baked into the initial design rationale. Eval 2 run1 lists 'Accessibility is considered' as one bullet in a post-design review checklist; run2 lists an 'accessibility audit' as a Gate 3 (post-code) item; run3 lists it as a checklist bullet. Eval 1 (the component-definition-process eval) mentions accessibility in only 1 of 3 runs, and only as a passing 'trade-off' ('Trade-offs: Performance, accessibility, browser support concerns' in run2) — runs 1 and 3 of eval 1 omit it entirely from the do/don't, states, and variants documentation they produce. This falls short of the skill's own bar of accessibility being 'baked into component definitions (not added later)'.

criteria.criterion: Regular audits comparing the design system to production are recommended as an ongoing governance practice.
criteria.evidence: All 3 eval 2 runs include a dedicated recurring-audit section: run1 '## 5. Regular Audits: System vs. Production... Every quarter, do this...'; run2 '## 5. Conduct Regular Production Audits... Quarterly or biannually...'; run3 '## 5. Audit Production Against System... Once a quarter (or monthly for a fast-moving product)...', each tying deviations found back into proposing new variants.

criteria.criterion: Tokens/values are named semantically (e.g. named scales, semantic icon names) rather than left as raw, unnamed values.
criteria.evidence: This is only surfaced inconsistently. In eval 0 (icons), only run2 includes the skill's semantic-naming guidance ('Name semantically: use arrow-right, chevron-down, check-circle, not icon-23'); run1 and run3 omit any naming guidance entirely, covering only size/color/stroke. No eval prompt or run addresses semantic color/spacing token naming (e.g. `color.action.primary` vs. raw `#0066FF`, or a named spacing scale like `space-md`) at all, despite this being an explicit 'What Good Looks Like' bullet and a worked example in the skill body.
